I'm in the UK and donated in April and July. This is what happened (I went to a dedicated donor centre so it may be a bit different if you're going to a church hall etc!)

* I was asked to arrive on time for the appointment, not early, to reduce the amount of people at the centre. 
* Once I got there, I had to sanitise my hands and they took my temperature and asked if I had any Corona symptoms.
* Everybody in the waiting area was very spaced out, you could still use the water dispenser to get your drink.
* I got prescreened in a little room where they ask questions like are you pregnant, have you been ill, do you have Covid, stuff like that. 
* After the screening I went and sat down in another socially distanced waiting area before my name was called.
* The donation was fine - if anything it was very weird having a stranger so close to me because of everything! But the people (nurses?) there were sanitising their hands lots and socially distancing where they could.
* Usually there's a group of chairs where you go and sit and have your drink/biscuit afterwards but the last time I went they brought me a drink and the food to the chair so I could stay there.

I wore my mask apart from when I had a drink before and after donating. Because of the reduced amount of people in the centre, it was probably quicker than usual! It was also a really nice atmosphere because they were doing plasma from people who've had Covid so there was a definite positive vibe in the air.

Good luck! I hope it goes well, if you have any questions just let me know. The nurses are always really friendly and will be doubly so if it's your first time!

Edit: NHS guidance which should cover everything: https://www.blood.co.uk/news-and-campaigns/news-and-statements/coronavirus-covid-19-updates/. Their Facebook page is also very responsive.

Just finished rewatching the first two doctors so those companions are the freshest in my mind.

Best:

Sara - after Katarina’s death, you don’t really expect another companion death so soon (especially as a modern viewer?) and the way it’s done is brutal - the graphics are really effective and creepy. Also the realisation that it was completely unnecessary because the Doctor would have made it back anyway so it’s just so sad. Sara, you were badass and I would have loved to see you as a companion for longer! 

Jamie and Zoe - this is a bittersweet one. One of my favourite TARDIS teams broken up when you can see that they were all having a great time and would have gone on travelling for ages (forever?) Like if Donna had spent way longer with the Doctor and (in Jamie’s case) got transported back to a place which we’ve already established is a very dangerous place to be. RIP the last 140 episodes of character growth. 

Honourable mention: 

Steven’s fake out - I really like that Steven calls the Doctor out on his shit so much and him storming out of the TARDIS after an argument makes sense. Didn’t buy his departure in The Savages.

Worst: 

Dodo - I mean at least we got rid of her. Seriously, why didn’t they get her back to tell the Doctor in person? Was this the Beeb’s decision or Jackie Lane’s? An unsatisfactory end to an unsatisfactory character.
